newsitem.title: GERMANY: German employment chief sees jobless rising - papers.
newsitem.headline: German employment chief sees jobless rising - papers.

text.p: Bernhard Jagoda, head of the office that publishes Germany's jobless figures, was quoted in newspapers on Saturday as saying unemployment could rise to 4.5 million by next February.

Jagoda, president of the German Labour Office, was quoted in an advance copy of Sunday's Bild am Sonntag newspaper as warning that such a figure was likely "if the economy does not do anything and the winter is hard".
German unemployment in November reached a post-unification record of 4.1 million on a seasonally-adjusted basis, with 3.94 out of work on a non-adjusted calculation.

In the Cologne-based Express newspaper, Jagoda was also quoted as saying jobless levels were set to rise "significantly" above four million over the winter, but as forecasting a year average of 3.95 million.
Jagoda's Labour Office was told by German finance minister Theo Waigel in November that wider budgetary demands would mean deep cuts in its funding, which is used for job creation and other projects.
Jagoda said that if unemployment turned out to be higher than he forecast, the Labour Office with its reduced budget would simply not be able to function properly.
Jagoda nonetheless insisted that a previously-stated government goal of halving unemployment by the year 2000 was still possible "but only if we act quickly".

In an advance copy of an interview in the Magdeburg-based "Volkstimme am Sonntag", he renewed calls for measures such as increased part-time working, lower levels of overtime and moderation in wage bargaining.
